narrative.overview: Kr4ftLabs should feel like an independent maker's workshop with its doors open: purposeful, exact, and visibly alive. The interface combines editorial-scale typography with the structural honesty of a technical catalogue. Warm paper keeps the system approachable; charcoal gives it authority; vivid orange behaves like a live electrical signal. This is a product ecosystem, not a startup template. Every section should clarify what is being built, what state it is in, or what the maker values. The lightning mark supplies energy through angular cuts, offsets, line work, and tightly controlled motion—not through glows, gradients, or ornamental effects.
keyCharacteristics: Monumental, tightly tracked typography with compact supporting copy.
Alternating charcoal, warm-paper, and signal-orange chapter surfaces.
Sharp containers, one-pixel rules, hard offsets, circles, and angular brand geometry.
Honest product states and task-focused previews instead of invented proof.
Purposeful motion that reveals structure and always respects reduced-motion preferences.

rules.name: The Live Wire Rule
rules.body: Orange must carry meaning. It may own a deliberate chapter band, but inside mixed layouts it marks action, status, progress, or the brand's lightning energy.

rules.name: The Warm Neutral Rule
rules.body: Do not replace the paper tones with pure white or the charcoal with generic blue-black. Their warmth is what keeps the technical language human.

rules.name: The Two-Voice Rule
rules.body: Geist speaks for ideas and actions; Geist Mono speaks for state, metadata, and system signals. Do not introduce a third type family without a brand-level decision.

rules.name: The Tight-When-Loud Rule
rules.body: The larger the headline, the tighter its tracking and leading. Body copy never inherits the compressed display treatment.

rules.name: The Chapter Rhythm Rule
rules.body: Each major section must change scale, surface, or composition enough to feel like a new chapter while retaining the same tokens and geometry.

rules.name: The One-Pixel Grid Rule
rules.body: Dense catalogues and repeated panels are separated by a one-pixel ink gap or rule—not by floating-card spacing and shadows.

rules.name: The Hard Shadow Rule
rules.body: A shadow must read as a printed offset or physical layer. If it looks atmospheric, soft, or glowing, remove it.

rules.name: The Flat-at-Rest Rule
rules.body: Ordinary cards, navigation, and controls use no shadow. State changes rely on color, rule weight, translation, or geometry.

rules.name: The Edge Discipline Rule
rules.body: Keep primary containers and controls square. Do not soften the product into rounded SaaS chrome.

rules.name: The Circle Has a Job Rule
rules.body: Every circle should indicate status, orbit, navigation, or focus. Circles are not filler decoration.

rules.name: The Motion Proves Structure Rule
rules.body: Movement should show hierarchy, progress, or spatial relation. Do not add idle spectacle that competes with product meaning.

dos: Do use the supplied Kr4ftLabs wordmark, symbol, and adaptive app icons; keep the written brand name exactly “Kr4ftLabs.”
Do make the first viewport immediately state that this is a maker-led home for useful digital products.
Do alternate bold chapter surfaces while keeping tokens, line work, and typography consistent.
Do show what a tool helps someone accomplish, and pair every real product with an honest availability state.
Do use angular geometry, hard offsets, and directional motion to echo the lightning mark.
Do verify every composition at 1440px and 375px, with keyboard focus and reduced motion included.
donts: Don't invent product names, destinations, metrics, testimonials, user counts, or performance claims.
Don't use decorative gradients, glassmorphism, bloom, excessive glow, or soft floating shadows.
Don't default to repetitive rounded feature cards, pill-heavy controls, or a generic startup hero.
Don't flood mixed layouts with orange; reserve it for meaningful signals or a deliberately committed chapter surface.
Don't treat the logo as a watermark or repeat lightning motifs until they overpower content.
Don't add a third font, stock illustration style, or unrelated icon family without a deliberate extension of the system.
